newsitem.title: USA: ADM holder says plea shows need for reform.
newsitem.headline: ADM holder says plea shows need for reform.

text.p: The California Public Employees Retirement System (CalPERS), which holds about 3.5 million shares of Archer Daniels Midland Co, said a settlement reached by ADM with the Justice Department provides support for its proposal to reform ADM'S directors and practices.
Earlier today, Decatur, Illinois-based agribusiness giant ADM said it agreed to pay $100 million in fines and plead guilty to price fixing in the food additives business.

"The $100 million fine is shareholder assets that are being squandered to pay for criminal activity that should have never occurred," James Burton, chief executive officer of CalPERS, said in a statement.
"Again we ask the question, where was the board of directors?" he said.

"That's why this admission of guilt is a compelling reason to reform the board and its practices. It speaks volumes to supporting our proposal to change the bylaws to require a truly independent board of directors. This $100 million is real money, which could have been used in many ways to improve the company's profitability," he said in a statement.

CalPERS and the Florida Retirement System Trust Fund have proposed that a change in ADM's bylaws be voted on at ADM's October 17 annual shareholders meeting in Decatur. The proposal requires that independent directors have a majority on the company's board.
The Florida pension fund holds about three million ADM shares.
